instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Admit You Need Me
cards.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cupboard's leaning because the back panel is upside down. Please stop tightening it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm following the diagram.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The arrow marked 'top' is pointing at your shoes. I'll turn the panel; you hold the sides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you do the sides too? I can't keep them square.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Ask me to assemble it with you. We're rather past 'just checking the diagram.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the timer setting, not the temperature. Let me get the heater working.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can manage. Just tell me which button.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Press 'mode' once. Then the number with the little degree sign is the temperature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says eighteen, but it's still cold. Should I press it again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Eighteen is the room temperature. Please ask me to help with the heating before we schedule it for eighteen o'clock.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your train, taste the soup from this clean spoon. We don't judge seasoning from the cooking ladle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One pinch, then stir and taste again. You can't approve an adjustment you haven't tasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have eight minutes to get to the station.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A teaspoonful, then. Blow on it first. I need a verdict on the soup, not on how hot the spoon is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you zip the suitcase, the jam needs a sealed bag. Wool absorbs a leak; it doesn't contain it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wrapped it twice in my jumper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twice gives you two sticky sleeves. Take it out and I'll check the lid before we pack it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the jar here. Problem solved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not until we've checked your jumper. Unfold it, please; jam doesn't stop travelling because the jar does.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can have tea once we've repaired this properly. A nod isn't an apology.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you're upset.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a report on my mood. Try a sentence with something you did in it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry if I did anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remove 'if' and 'anything.' I'll keep the tea warm while you find the actual sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. We need a complete apology before I open the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I sent you a thumbs-up. That meant we were fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It meant your thumb was raised. Remorse requires a sentence, preferably spoken to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Mistakes were made.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An excellent passive construction. Now try 'I made a mistake.' We've still got nine minutes.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your approval for opening up the pond edge. Willow roots and a liner are not a happy partnership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The willow gives us shade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shade doesn't patch a liner. I've taken the willow out before it reached the new pond.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean you cut it down without asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. We can replace shade; we can't ask a root to go round a liner. Will you approve the clearance?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your agreement to dinner for six. We can serve it as a buffet; seated service needs more than two chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, people can stand with the soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with bowls and nowhere to put them. I've invited them for seven o'clock, so I'll change the soup to something they can eat with one hand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've already invited them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. The invitations are settled; the menu is correctable. Can I have your yes while there is still time to cook?

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These eighty place cards would give your lettering proper practice. Keep the capitals on one line and they'll look quite accomplished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like calligraphy. I don't want to copy eighty names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read them aloud. You can concentrate on a consistent slant; that's the part your samples need.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She confuses black ink with good lettering. Choose your purple; I'll correct my aunt. Would you like the broad nib?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sorting this shed would give you a proper workshop. Heavy tins belong below waist height; the bench is for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll just put your paint on the bench again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll mark a paint shelf. One shelf, not every flat surface. You could finally leave your tools laid out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including a part of the bench you're forbidden to use?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A work zone, yes. Mark its edge properly and I'll keep my paint outside it. Would you like the whole left side?
